intro: Leaks are one of those problems that rarely announce themselves clearly. In Crichton, where many homes have been standing for well over a century, a slow drip behind a wall or a hidden pipe weeping under a floor can cause serious damage long before you notice any obvious signs. Whether you've spotted a damp patch, an unexplained rise in your water bill, or you can simply hear water running when everything should be off, getting a professional leak detection survey done promptly is the sensible move. Catching a leak early in Crichton almost always means the difference between a modest repair bill and a costly renovation involving floors, walls, or structural timberwork.
localContext: Crichton's housing stock tells the story of several different eras of construction, and each comes with its own leak-related quirks. The older stone-built properties and period cottages that make up much of the village often have original or part-original pipework — lead, iron, or early copper — that has simply reached the end of its serviceable life. These older pipes are more prone to pinhole corrosion and joint failures, particularly where they pass through solid stone walls with little room for movement. Modern estate homes in Crichton face a different but equally real set of issues: plastic push-fit fittings can work loose over time, and underfloor heating systems occasionally develop slow weeps that go unnoticed for months. Crichton sits in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale gradually builds up inside pipes and at joints, putting extra stress on seals and increasing the likelihood of leaks developing around boiler connections, radiator valves, and under-sink pipework. Taken together, the local property mix means leak detection calls here cover a wide range of pipe types, ages, and access challenges.
serviceDetail: When a plumber arrives at your Crichton property for a leak detection visit, the process is more methodical than most people expect. It isn't simply a case of turning up and looking around — modern leak detection uses a combination of specialist equipment and plumber expertise to pinpoint problems without unnecessary damage to your home. The job typically begins with a visual inspection of all accessible pipework, checking for obvious corrosion, staining, or damp. If the source isn't immediately obvious, the plumber will use one or more detection methods depending on what's suspected. Thermal imaging cameras can identify cold or damp patches behind walls and under floors without any cutting or drilling. Acoustic listening equipment picks up the faint sound of water escaping from pressurised pipes, even when buried in concrete or solid walls. For suspected underground leaks, tracer gas testing is sometimes used — a harmless gas is introduced into the pipework and a sensor detects where it escapes at ground level. Once the leak is found, the plumber will explain exactly what they've found, where it is, and what the repair options are before any work begins. Repairs in Crichton homes can range from straightforward joint replacements and section re-pipes to more involved work accessing pipes beneath floors or behind stone walls. You'll always be given a clear explanation before anything is opened up.
pricing: Leak detection in Crichton typically costs between £100 and £200 for a standard survey, depending on how much of the property needs to be investigated and which detection methods are required. Simple accessible leaks — a dripping joint under a sink or a visible pipe crack — can be repaired for £100 to £150 including parts. More involved repairs, such as replacing a corroded section of pipework inside a stone wall or addressing a leak in a buried supply pipe, usually fall in the £250 to £500 range once access work and reinstatement are included. Older properties in Crichton with original pipework sometimes reveal additional issues once a repair is underway, so it's worth asking your plumber for an honest assessment of what else they spot while they're in. Most will flag this up rather than leave you to discover it later.
whyLocal: Choosing a plumber who knows Crichton and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely matters for this kind of work. Local tradespeople are familiar with the older stone construction methods used across the village, they understand the quirks of properties that have been extended and re-plumbed multiple times over the decades, and they know the typical supply pipe routes and water pressure characteristics in the area. That local knowledge often saves time during detection work and avoids unnecessary damage. A tradesperson who regularly works in Crichton will also be easier to get back quickly if a follow-up visit is needed, which counts for a lot when you're dealing with an active leak.

faqs.q: How do I know if I have a hidden leak in my Crichton home?
faqs.a: The most common signs are a water bill that's risen without explanation, damp patches on walls or ceilings, the sound of running water when taps and appliances are off, or soft spots in floorboards or plaster. In Crichton's older stone properties, external wall damp is sometimes mistaken for condensation when it's actually a slow internal pipe leak — worth having checked if it persists.

faqs.q: Will the plumber need to break through my walls or floors to find the leak?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Thermal imaging and acoustic detection equipment can locate most leaks without any cutting or drilling. If the leak is confirmed to be inside a wall or under a floor, some access will be needed to make the repair, but a good plumber will keep this to the minimum required and will always discuss it with you beforehand.

faqs.q: My Crichton cottage has original lead pipework — is that more of a concern?
faqs.a: Lead pipes are more prone to corrosion and joint failure as they age, so leaks in older Crichton properties with original pipework are not uncommon. Beyond the leak itself, it's also worth discussing replacement with your plumber, as lead pipework can affect water quality. Many Midlothian properties have had lead supply pipes replaced in recent years, and it's a job worth considering.

faqs.q: How quickly can a leak detection appointment be arranged in Crichton?
faqs.a: For an active leak causing damage, most local plumbers serving Crichton can attend the same day or next day. For a suspected slow leak where there's no immediate risk, a booked appointment within a few days is typical. It's always worth calling sooner rather than later — slow leaks can cause significant hidden damage to timbers and insulation over weeks and months.
